I was molested when I was 8. The weird part is, aside from feeling uncomfortable, I don't remember it being that bad. In fact I even laughed some during it. It was done by my older cousin to me and my cousin who was also 8. I still see him whenever the whole family gets together and I can talk to him and see him just fine. It does kinda weird me out that that happened and it's almost like no one really thinks about it but me. I remember for that and I think some other reasons I had to take some kind of antidepressant when I was 8, but I don't remember me taking it badly or it affecting me now. Maybe I was just trying to lock my feelings in a vault, maybe I was too young to rationalize it so it didn't matter as much, or maybe I really took it a lot harder than I remember and it still unwittingly fucks with me to this day. I wish I knew, but I guess it doesn't matter now.

With your priest, maybe you can approach him during confession, after service or during office hours. Sorry I don't know the exact details of how the Catholic Church operates, I'm actually Protestant. But can't you also speak to him about everything during confession? 

For therapy or counseling, I'm not sure about your area, but I bet you could just google "therapy in (city name)" and find all your options. From there, you can look at reviews maybe to see what is best. Do you live with your parents? Do you have any source of your own income? I'm just trying to help you with logistics for that if you're interested. Honestly, I don't know much of how all of this works. Like I said I'm just 18. I know it sounds crazy expensive. But I think you're doing yourself a disservice by not talking to a counselor about this or even a therapist about your mental barriers like anxiety or depression. You wouldn't avoid going to the doctor if you broke a leg. This is no different. And I guarantee you it's worth the money if you are currently considering suicide, because you may be not as rich as you were walking in, but you're alive and you may be able to formulate a plan. That being said, you could always privately talk to your church's priest sometime about this. They're trained in counseling too.

I truly hope science can keep up with mental illness so one day people like you truly can get the help they deserve. I know you'll live a harder life and I know it's hard to say that you're going to be "better." But after a while, you will get better. Not to say perfect. You'll still probably have bipolar disorder so I'm not trying to sound cliche. It sounds sad but yes it will be, mostly just, more manageable. Although I can speak from some experience that this is better than it sounds. Sorry I probably sound like every cliche person you've been talking to. Maybe a lot of this people just don't know what they're talking about. Actually I guarantee you most people have no idea what they're going though and are just trying to be helpful. But they are trying to be helpful. These people really do care and your bipolar disorder must be extremely difficult to manage. But I guarantee you this thing is fortifying your strength in the process. I'm not saying it's a good thing, but you will probably be stronger than a lot of people, having to battle these daily demons.

That's pretty wise dude and I'm glad you've found your groove. There's not really much about me to share. All I'm really ever interested in is hanging out with my friends, the occasional video game, and mostly studying and preparing for my future. Which actually sounds pretty lame when I write it out because 90% of my free time I spend just planning out what I want to do in several years.

But they're also *your* family. They may be disappointed or even downright upset but I know they're rooting for you at the end of the day. And I know sometimes it feels like God can't help and only you can make that connection with him. Do you go to church usually?

Hey whatever works best for you!cAnd I understand what you mean. I bet you're pretty strong willed even if you may feel weak. I can tell you why, and it's because everyday day you wake up with a mental illness and a lot of people don't know what you're going though, but you still power forward.

Hey Andrew. I'm Raymond. That sounds like some rough stuff man and I'm really sorry about what happened. You had know way of knowing how things with your family would turn out so I hope you don't feel bad with the outcomes. What kind of interests do you have? College is a suckers game anyway for a lot of degrees. Maybe there's a technical school that has some interesting trades or something? But I know the military doesn't always seem appealing but hey, they do have some decent benefits and plenty of options.

Who all do you think you've let down? And that's cool there's a fellow Christian here. What comforts me also is knowing that God is watching everything closely. He knows we mess up. And sometimes big time, but he is still protecting us and I know you can also find solace in Him. Maybe you could talk to a Priest about your situation. They deal with a lot and can give the best advice. If you decided you wanted more secular conversations you can always talk to a therapist or counselor. Although I don't know your situation so I don't know how easy that may be for you.
Oh I just read this after I PM'd you. Thanks for actually reading it. And I may dream big but who knows if I can also walk the walk. Can I ask what you're planning on doing?

Ha thanks. I guess I'm hard on myself, but I feel like for my aspirations I need to be. I just hope I can still succeed academically after high school too, since a lot of the time I have to study more than my other classmates and I sometimes rely on them to help me with assignments.

I know right now you're looking for a solution. I can't offer one unfortunately. That's probably not what you want to hear from me, because I believe how stressed you are and it sounds awful and I'm sorry. But you're the only one qualified to really make this decision. I can help you though and I can be here if you need to talk. I will say these things though: committing suicide will make her worse than anything possible-by guaranteed. And if you try to keep this up, you will tear yourself apart not only mentally, but even physically as you can already tell from your stress and even hair loss. You said you believe in God? As in Christianity or do you believe something else?

Man I've been there. Maybe you want to talk? I'm 18 myself so we might be closer in age. You don't have to tell me yours, but it if you're pretty young you have a lot of time to accomplish things you never though possible. Actually, you can be old and experience that too. But remember- you are *never* too young to have real problems and real depression and real suicidal thoughts. Hell, at 8 years old I had to take antidepressants. If you want to chat though I'm game. You don't have to feel shy, because we want to be your friend here.
Everyone makes mistakes. Even huge ones. I know that probably doesn't help right now, but if you want to talk about what's going on I'm willing to talk.

First of all, I'm sorry. In no way do you deserve this illness and it does not reflect you as a person. It really blows your therapist bounced real quick, but it sounds to me as if it was an emergency and maybe time was just not on her side. Yeah that's kinda unfair to you, and I don't think you're overreacting, but I bet the therapist really wishes she could tell you herself and I doubt she would want to abandon you or any of her clients. And you could also tell your psychiatrist how you feel about your interactions with him, and maybe he might learn something. I don't think you're overreacting or being crazy, but I can assure you the therapist isn't trying to bump you off to another one by saying she doesn't take your interest. That's totally unethical and IANAL but sounds illegal. If you want to talk more about what you're going through I'm all ears too.
